name: Standing Cable Chest Press
cues: Set the pulleys just above shoulder height and step forward into a split stance
Brace your core and lean slightly into the press
Press the handles forward and together at chest height
Let your elbows travel back slowly until your hands reach your chest

qa.note: Approved by the owner 2026-10-09 (bulk approval of waves 3b and 3c). Earlier findings, kept for follow-up: Wave 3b 2026-10-09: rated minor, owner review. needs work: The joint-space lerp gives a fly-like arc, not a press. From lockout (hands y 127, x ±20) the hands swing out to x ±47 with the elbow only 36 deg bent, then rise to y 150 at u 0.375, 11 cm above the shoulder joint (y 139). At the bottom the hands are at x ±41 (18 cm outside the shoulders) and 26 cm in front of them, not at the chest. Elbows sit at shoulder height (elev 80, plane -18) against the template's own '~45-60 deg' comment. With pulleys at x ±1.12 / z 0.1, the bottom pull is 70 cm sideways vs 28 cm back, so the load is mostly a fly. | minor: Fixed: the joint-space lerp is gone. The left hand is now solved with attachHand along a straight, level line at chest height, about 11 cm below the shoulder joint all rep, and the right arm mirrors it. At the bottom the hand is at x 27, 4 cm outside the shoulder joint, about 6 cm in front of the chest. The upper arm is 52-55 deg out (plane -11). Lockout: hands 17 cm apart, elbow 7. The pulleys moved behind the lifter to x ±0.70, z -0.30, which is about 0.5 m behind the shoulders, so the bottom pull is now mostly back (43 cm out vs 70 cm back). New tests cover the level path, hands staying below the shoulders, bottom width, arm elevation 40-62, and the pulley offset and direction. Remaining: no pulley spot behind the lifter at chest height cleared the arm. They now sit at y 1.62, about 22 cm above the shoulder joint, so I changed cue 1 to 'just above shoulder height' in EN and UK (UK needs a native check). At lockout the cable still grazes the forearm at -8.3 mm against the 10 mm cable tolerance, so there is little margin. In the side sheet the cable runs close over the deltoid at the bottom.
